_note: Inputs for backend/src/scripts/ironwoodEnergy.ts. Every value carries its source, date and working.

phase1_mw.method: The case gives a 480 MW initial substation; the real Upper Mount Bethel filings show a 480 MW on-site substation.

full_build_mw.method: The case gives up to 2,000 MW at full build; the real MOU targets 2 gigawatts.

load_factor.method: The campus is taken to draw its full peak in every hour, the same convention leepr's cost runs use, so the two sets of figures agree. A real campus averages somewhat less, which would scale every annual figure down in proportion.

discount_rate.method: KGE's 10% investment threshold, from the case.

gas_capex_usd_per_kw.method: Onsite gas is priced as a reciprocating engine plant, the technology data centers buy for islanded supply (Wärtsilä's 412 MW, 40-engine order for an Ohio hyperscale campus, Power Engineering 16 Apr 2026). EIA AEO2020 capital cost report, Case 4, four 5.6 MW engines: $1,810/kW in 2019 dollars, the latest EIA engine case. Low $1,700/kW is the Wärtsilä 18V50SG screening cost in NYISO's 2025-2029 demand curve reset (Burns & McDonnell, Dec 2023). High $2,400/kW is the market quote S&P Global reported for new gas plants in May 2025.

gas_heat_rate_btu_per_kwh.method: EIA AEO2020 Case 4 reciprocating engines, 8,295 Btu/kWh. NYISO's Wärtsilä 18V50SG screening figure agrees at 8,290 Btu/kWh HHV.

gas_plant_life_years.method: Recovered over the customer's 20-year power agreement rather than Lazard's 30-year plant life, because the plant exists to serve that contract.

gas_redundancy_factor.unit: installed MW per MW of load
gas_redundancy_factor.method: An islanded campus needs spare engines so one can be down for maintenance or a fault without dropping load. 15% spare capacity is an assumption; no published standard was found.

gas_capacity_factor.method: Delivered energy per kW of campus load, equal to the load factor.

gas_price_usd_per_mmbtu.method: EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook (6 Oct 2026) Henry Hub forecast for 2026, $3.48/MMBtu. Low is the 2027 forecast, $3.16. High is the price Pennsylvania industrial users paid in 2024, $9.19/Mcf (EIA), divided by 1.037 MMBtu per Mcf = $8.86/MMBtu. A plant tapping an interstate pipeline in eastern Pennsylvania would pay between the two.

gas_co2_lb_per_mmbtu.method: EIA carbon dioxide emissions coefficient for natural gas, 116.65 lb CO2/MMBtu. EPA's 2025 factor (53.06 kg = 117.0 lb) agrees.

gas_years_to_power.method: Wärtsilä's 412 MW engine order for an Ohio data center, placed in April 2026, targets commercial operation in early 2028, about two years. Value adds half a year for Pennsylvania air permitting. Low 2 years is that Ohio schedule. High 5 years is the average wait for a large gas turbine in 2025 (Wood Mackenzie via Utility Dive, 24 Feb 2026), the fallback if engines are not used.

battery_capex_usd_per_kwh.method: NREL, Cost Projections for Utility-Scale Battery Storage: 2025 Update, 4-hour system in 2024: $334/kWh (2024$). Low is NREL's 2030 low projection, $207/kWh. High is the top of Lazard LCOS 2026's initial capital range, $365/kWh.

battery_fixed_om_share.method: NREL ATB 2024: fixed O&M at 2.5% of capital cost per year.

grid_price_usd_per_mwh.method: The same Pennsylvania industrial average leepr uses for Ironwood: 9.36 cents per kWh in 2025 (EIA). Low 8.51 cents is the cheapest 2025 month; high 11.04 cents is July 2026, the latest month published. A retail industrial rate already includes energy, capacity and delivery.

grid_connection_years.method: Read from the us-pa-northampton entry of regions.json so the two models agree. Value: Electrical Contractor (17 Aug 2026), citing JLL's 2026 Global Data Center Outlook, puts the national average wait to power a data center at four years, up from 12-18 months in 2022. High: up to seven years in Dominion's Northern Virginia territory, also PJM (Bloomberg via Data Center Knowledge, Aug 2024). Low is an inference, not a published figure: PPL's president told the PA Senate GOP Policy Committee (11 Aug 2025) that construction often begins 6-12 months after a 45-60 day feasibility study. Replaces the 3.2-year LBNL generator-queue proxy every PJM region shares. Amazon dropped this same site in 2025 citing 'the lack of available power' (WFMZ, 29 Apr 2025).

grid_co2_lb_per_mwh.method: EPA eGRID2023 (Rev 2, Jun 2025), RFC East subregion, CO2 total output emission rate 596.9 lb/MWh. High is the same table's non-baseload rate, 1,175.6 lb/MWh, which describes the plants that ramp up to serve new load and is the better guide to what an added campus actually causes.

capacity_price_usd_per_mw_day.method: PJM Base Residual Auction for 2028/29, the first year Ironwood could plausibly take power: PPL zone and RTO cleared at $325.00/MW-day, the price cap. Low is 2025/26 at $269.92; high is 2027/28 at $333.44, also the cap. Met-Ed takes the MAAC price, equal to the RTO price in every one of these auctions.

wholesale_energy_usd_per_mwh.method: PJM Independent Market Monitor, 2025 State of the Market: load-weighted average real-time LMP $50.73/MWh in 2025. Low is 2024, $33.74. High is January to August 2026, $74.06 (IMM presentation, 28 Sep 2026).

ppa_price_usd_per_mwh.method: LevelTen Energy PPA Price Index, PJM solar P25 in Q4 2025: $81.03/MWh, as reported by pv magazine USA (30 Jan 2026). No PJM figure for a 2026 quarter is public. Low is LevelTen's North American solar P25 for Q2 2026, $52.65; high is the Q2 2026 market-averaged wind index, $83.79 (pv-tech, 23 Jul 2026). Solar is used as the available benchmark; it is not the clean firm power the GRID standard asks for, which no public price index covers.

clean_contract_share.method: Sized to the 32% clean firm share Pennsylvania's GRID Standards require from 1 Jan 2035, so the contracted share meets the state's final step from the start.

clean_firm_2027.method: PA GRID Standards: incremental capacity located in the same PJM deliverability area must include clean firm energy of 10.0% beginning 1 January 2027. The page does not define clean firm.

clean_firm_2030.method: PA GRID Standards: incremental capacity located in the same PJM deliverability area must include clean firm energy of 14.5% beginning 1 January 2030. The page does not define clean firm.

clean_firm_2035.method: PA GRID Standards: incremental capacity located in the same PJM deliverability area must include clean firm energy of 32.0% beginning 1 January 2035. The page does not define clean firm.

curtailment_event_hours.method: The battery carries the whole campus for 4 hours, the standard utility battery size. Duke's "Rethinking Load Growth" (Norris et al., Feb 2025) finds the average curtailment event lasts 1.7 hours at 0.25% annual curtailment and 2.1 hours at 0.5%, so 4 hours covers roughly twice the average event.

curtailment_share_of_energy.method: Duke's 0.5% curtailment case, where PJM alone could absorb about 18 GW of new flexible load, averaging 177 curtailed hours a year across the 22 balancing authorities studied.

flexible_peak_reduction_share.method: During a grid emergency the battery carries the full campus, so the campus draws nothing from PJM in those hours. A load that is off the grid at the system peak avoids the capacity charge tied to that peak. Under PJM's 16 Jan 2026 Board decision, new large loads without their own generation are curtailed before pre-emergency demand response, so a campus that can drop to zero on call fits the rule PJM has adopted.

flexible_years_saved.method: How much sooner a load that accepts curtailment can connect is not published. PJM's connect-and-manage decision lets large loads connect subject to curtailment before every upgrade is built, and its Expedited Interconnection Track runs 10 months for projects that bring generation. One year is an assumption; low is 0 and high is 2.

pjm_shortfall_2028_mw.method: PJM's 2028/29 Base Residual Auction cleared 6,831.3 MW short of the reliability requirement. Low is the 2027/28 shortfall, 6,623 MW, the first year PJM cleared short.
